---
title: "Start bridge (@tuturuuu/start-bridge)"
description: "The frozen v0 contract for running Next App Router satellites on TanStack Start + Vite+ on Cloudflare, including the basePath and per-app session cookie rules."
---

`@tuturuuu/start-bridge` is the shared layer that lets a satellite's existing
App Router source run under TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void on a Cloudflare
Worker. It replaces the per-app `src/runtime` shim copies in Meet, Mail and
Calendar. The core (`route-match`, `base-path`, `mounts`, `app-url`, `endpoints`,
`pages`, `api-forward`, `canary`, `csp`, `request-context/core`) has no React, Start or
Vite imports; the `next/*`, `start/*`, `intl/*` and `vite` entries are the
framework adapters at the edge.

This page is the **v0 API freeze**. App lanes convert against these export
paths and signatures. Within v0, changes are additive only: a new optional
option, a new export, or a new subpath. Removing or changing a frozen
signature needs a new subpath and a coordinated migration.

## Worker handler

```ts
import { createFunctionProxy } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/function-proxy';
import { createBridgeHandler } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/handler';
import { createBridgeStartHandler } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/server-entry';
import { proxy } from '../src/proxy';
import { endpoints } from '../src/runtime/api-registry.bridge.gen';

export default {
  fetch: createBridgeHandler<Env, ExecutionContext>({
    mounts: {
      app: 'meet',
      rootHosts: ['meet.tuturuuu.com'],
      mountHosts: ['tuturuuu.com'],
      basePath: '/meet',
    },
    start: createBridgeStartHandler(),
    serverFnBase: '/_serverFn',
    proxy,
    endpoints,
    functionBase: '/_serverFn',
    functionProxy: createFunctionProxy({ targetApp: 'meet' }),
    publicAssets,
    assets: (env) => env.ASSETS,
    centralApiOrigin: (env) => env.INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN ?? 'https://tuturuuu.com',
  }),
};
```

Order: base resolution from `mounts` (a mount host outside the mount is 404),
`/assets/*` and declared public files from `ASSETS` (base-stripped), then the
app's `proxy.ts`, `centralFirst` paths to the central API (Next `beforeFiles`
rewrites such as `TUTURUUU_WEB_WORKSPACE_API_RESERVED_PATHS`; Next sources
like `/api/v1/:wsId/x` or bracket patterns), the generated endpoint registry,
unowned `/api/*` to the central API (base-stripped), server functions to Start (base-stripped), and
finally pages to Start at the browser-visible URL. The response then gets
Location rewriting. Cookies pass through unchanged. A `proxy.ts` rewrite to
another origin throws unless that origin is the configured central API origin
(`rewriteOrigins`), which is then fetched with manual redirects and hop-by-hop
headers removed.

In the app: `start.ts` passes `serverFns: { fetch: bridgeServerFnFetch }` to
`createStart`, `getRouter()` sets `basepath: routerBasepath()` and
`ssr: { nonce: requestNonce() }`, and the root route lists
`appBaseHeadScript()` first in `head().scripts`. With `csp` set, every
response gets a fresh nonce in its `Content-Security-Policy`, which the router
and the head script repeat. On the apex the handler sits behind the one-origin
gate (`decideOneOriginRequest`, #6746).

## Registries and the unregistered-route check

Each app declares `start-bridge.routes.json` at its root:

```json
{
  "appDir": "src/app",
  "stripSegments": { "[locale]": { "locale": "en" } },
  "api": { "out": "src/runtime/api-registry.bridge.gen.ts" },
  "pages": { "out": "src/runtime/page-registry.bridge.gen.ts" },
  "owned": { "api/build-info/route.ts": "src/native/api.server.ts" },
  "ignored": { "api/legacy/route.ts": "served by the central API" }
}
```

`bun packages/start-bridge/src/codegen/cli.ts generate apps/<app>` writes the
registries; `check` fails when `appDir` is missing or not a directory (declare
`"appDir": null` for an app without App Router source), when a generated file is stale, a `route.*` or
`page.*` is neither generated, `owned` by an existing native file, nor
`ignored` with a reason, an `owned`/`ignored` entry names no file, two files
map to one URL shape (including `[id]` vs `[slug]`, or a page and a route), or a parallel/intercepting route appears. Route groups are
dropped from patterns. The page manifest exports `PagePattern`; type the page
model as `satisfies Record<PagePattern, Loader>` so a new page fails
type-check until it is handled. `*.bridge.gen.ts` files are excluded from
Biome.

## basePath contract

One compiled artifact serves an app at its subdomain root and mounted at
`tuturuuu.com/<app>`. The Worker resolves the base **per request** from the
host and path against `mounts` (`rootHosts` → `''`; `mountHosts` + the
`/<app>` prefix → `/<app>`; unlisted hosts default to the root, or 404 with
`unknownHost: 'reject'`). The build-time `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH` is only the
fallback when no runtime base exists. Root mode is the identity everywhere.

| Concern | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Ownership | A mount host owns `/<app>` and `/<app>/*` only; `/meetings` is not `/meet` |
| SSR | The request context carries `appBase`; `runtimeAppBase()` reads it per request |
| Hydration | `appBaseHeadScript()` serializes the base before the client router starts |
| Router | `basepath: routerBasepath()` (`/` or `/<app>`) |
| Assets | The SSR manifest's script/stylesheet URLs get the request's base (`createBridgeStartHandler`); JS-referenced asset URLs read the runtime base (`renderBuiltUrl`), CSS ones stay relative to their stylesheet; requests are fetched from `ASSETS` base-stripped |
| Server functions | Compiled against the root (`/_serverFn`); `bridgeServerFnFetch` sends them to `/<app>/_serverFn` in the browser, and the Worker strips the base before Start |
| Next middleware | `NextRequest` carries Next's `basePath`; `nextUrl.pathname` is app-relative and `nextUrl.clone()` redirects keep the base |
| Links and navigation | `next/link`, `useRouter().push/replace`, `redirect()` prefix path-absolute hrefs with the runtime base |
| URLs in app code | `appPath('/...')` and `appUrl('/share/...', origin?)` from `app-url` (worklets, Live, preview, download, share) |
| Browser `/api` calls | Web-owned `/api` stays relative: on the apex it reaches Web directly, on a subdomain the Worker forwards it. App-owned endpoints must use `createApiPath(appApiPatterns, centralFirst)` (codegen `api.patternsOut` emits `appApiPatterns` without importing route modules); `@tuturuuu/internal-api` adapters register the same route-aware resolver for calls without client options |
| Location headers | Path-relative `Location` not already under the base gains it. Absolute URLs are never rewritten, so `new URL('/login', request.url)` behaves as in Next (it leaves the app) |
| Central API | Unowned `/<app>/api/*` is forwarded as `/api/*` |
| Auth return URLs | `appUrl(path, origin)` so the central login returns into the app |
| Cookies | Never renamed or path-scoped. The canonical session cookie is `tuturuuu_app_session` (+ `tuturuuu_app_session_refresh`) everywhere; there is no per-app name. Subdomains keep today's behaviour until cutover; the apex uses the shared session below |

`tuturuuu.com/meet` is the Meet app root; product marketing moves to
`/products/<app>`.

### Internal API resolver registration

`registerDefaultAppBaseResolver(resolver)` is exported from
`@tuturuuu/internal-api/client` and the package root. The callback receives a
normalized path and returns a relative mounted path or an absolute URL. Clients,
the shared singleton, `resolveInternalApiUrl(path, baseUrl?)`, and app-origin
helpers use this precedence for relative inputs: explicit per-call `baseUrl` >
client `options.baseUrl` > per-client `appBaseResolver` > latest active registered
default > built-in fallback. Explicit bases bypass both resolvers, including
resolvers returning absolute SSR URLs. Absolute input URLs bypass all base
resolution. With no registration, existing root and subdomain defaults remain.

Register once in each app adapter entrypoint, before requests or hydration.
Browser adapters can register `appPath`, or `createApiPath(appApiPatterns,
centralFirst)` when they also call Web-owned routes. The resolver applies to all
relative internal-api calls, so mixed consumers must select their app-owned
routes rather than prefix every route indiscriminately.

Server adapters must return an absolute URL using the incoming request host;
a mounted relative path alone would still resolve against the configured Web
origin. Read the bridge context inside the callback on every invocation:

```ts
import { registerDefaultAppBaseResolver } from '@tuturuuu/internal-api/client';
import { appUrl } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/app-url';
import { bridgeRequest } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/request-context';

const unregister = registerDefaultAppBaseResolver((path) =>
  appUrl(path, bridgeRequest().request.url)
);
```

This example addresses all calls to the incoming app host; adapters with central
Web calls must apply their ownership policy in the callback. Never register a
new resolver per request or close over one request's URL or base. The portable
internal-api module stores callbacks only; the bridge owns request isolation.
The returned unregister function is idempotent, supports out-of-order cleanup,
and restores the latest registration that is still active. Use it for adapter
teardown or hot reload.

Regression coverage: `packages/internal-api/src/default-app-base-resolver.test.ts`
executes root, Meet and Mail mounts, SSR host selection, interleaved bridge
requests sharing one client, per-client precedence, unregister, absolute bypass
and prefix-once behavior. Consumer runtime acceptance remains with each app.

## Shared session on the apex: decision (b), server-held session

**Decision (user, 2026-10-26):** every app mounted at `tuturuuu.com/<app>`
shares one Tuturuuu session that page script cannot read. It is an `HttpOnly`,
`Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie served through a backend-for-frontend (BFF)
session layer, with no JavaScript-readable access or refresh token anywhere. CSP
and Trusted Types stay mandatory per app, but as defense in depth, not the gate.
Apex cutovers stay held until the admission gate below reports ready.
Subdomain hosts keep serving throughout. The product rules (logout scope,
step-up, token lifetimes) are in
[Shared session](/platform/architecture/shared-session).

### Model

- **One writer.** Web is the only component that creates, refreshes, rotates or
  clears the session cookie. Mounted Workers and satellites on the apex only
  read it: they validate the JWT and derive per-app claims in memory per request
  (as `sessionMode: 'supabase-first'` already does). They never write or clear
  `sb-*`, `tuturuuu_app_session*` or `tuturuuu_web_app_session*`.
- **No token in JavaScript.** No access or refresh JWT is readable by page
  script, returned in a JSON body to a browser request, or kept in Web Storage,
  IndexedDB or the Cache API. The only exceptions are single-purpose
  capabilities that are topic- or object-scoped, last at most 5 minutes and
  cannot be exchanged for a session: realtime join tickets (60 s) and storage
  signed URLs.
- **Browser code reaches data only through same-origin `/api/*`** (or the app's
  own `/<app>/api/*`) with the cookie. Browser Supabase clients are retired.
- **Bearer clients are untouched.** A request with `Authorization: Bearer` is
  authenticated by the bearer alone; its cookies are ignored and CSRF rules do
  not apply. Mobile and CLI keep their native flows.
- **Mounted mode comes from the URL.** The bridge deletes any client-sent
  `x-tuturuuu-app-base` and sets its own from the resolved mount; auth code never
  trusts that header (#6774).
- **Stages.** Stage A makes the existing `sb-<ref>-auth-token*` cookie
  `HttpOnly` and keeps `Domain=.tuturuuu.com` so subdomain servers keep reading
  it; ambiguous duplicate cookies are treated as unauthenticated for unsafe
  methods. Stage B moves to a host-only `__Host-` cookie after the first
  cutovers.
- **End state.** The platform is moving to Cloudflare. The long-term session is
  a first-party signed `HttpOnly` cookie issued and verified in a Worker, with
  state in a Durable Object or D1. Supabase Auth becomes one identity provider
  behind an interface. Stage A and Stage B harden today's cookie in the
  meantime; build no new features on the Supabase cookie format.

### Mounted no-writer guard

The function-proxy change (#6774) covers server-function middleware only. The
app's ordinary `proxy.ts` and endpoint registry still reach the auth writers,
for example `/api/auth/verify-app-token` and `/api/auth/refresh-app-session`,
whose `createPOST` and `createRefreshPOST`
(`packages/auth/src/cross-app/server.ts`) set `Path=/` app-session cookies.
Under (b) the guard is permanent:

1. **Bridge admission**, before `proxy.ts` and endpoint dispatch: a mounted
   request (non-empty URL-derived `appBase`) to a session-minting endpoint gets a
   terminal `409 APP_SESSION_MOUNTED`, with no verification, rotation or
   `Set-Cookie`. A same-origin mount needs no handshake, because the apex
   cookie is the session.
2. **The writers themselves**: the app-session setters and
   `clearAppSessionCookie` refuse to write when the server-side bridge context
   is mounted (never a header). This also covers `proxy.ts` refresh and MFA
   redirects.
3. **Response backstop**: mounted responses drop any `Set-Cookie` for app-session
   **and Supabase session** names, and drop `Service-Worker-Allowed`.
4. **Logout** from a mounted app is a POST to Web `/api/auth/logout`.
5. **Expiry**: a mounted Worker answers `401 SESSION_REFRESH_REQUIRED` for API
   and server-function calls, and `303` to Web's refresh endpoint for document
   navigations. It never refreshes itself.

Whole-handler tests run through `createBridgeHandler`:

- mounted verify and refresh return `409` with no `Set-Cookie`;
- mounted pages and APIs emit no session `Set-Cookie`, including on the MFA and
  refresh-failure paths;
- root-mode controls behave exactly as today;
- a client-sent `x-tuturuuu-app-base` never switches modes.

### CSRF

Cookie-authenticated unsafe requests (no `Authorization: Bearer`) pass only
with `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, or, when Fetch Metadata is absent, an
`Origin` equal to the request's own origin. `same-site` (sibling subdomains),
`cross-site`, `none`, a missing or `null` `Origin` and any mismatch are
rejected. The check is a framework-free helper applied by Web middleware, by
bridge admission and by each BFF auth endpoint, with an explicit, tested
exemption registry (provider webhooks, OAuth callbacks, bearer and native auth
routes). It rolls out `off`, then `report` (at least 24 h clean in production),
then `enforce`, with the mode injected by each adapter.

### Admission gate

`@tuturuuu/utils/one-origin-routing` refuses the shared origin in every mode
until a `bffSessionReady` input is true. That input requires CSRF `enforce`, the
`HttpOnly` cookie, no browser Supabase client and the no-writer guard, read from
runtime config. Each app still needs its own one-origin admission review (CSP,
Trusted Types, content inventory).

## Page adapter

The generic App Router page adapter (React Server Components) and the
`'use server'` path are owned by the conversion codemod in
[#6760](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/6760), which also owns the
RSC-environment shims for `next-intl/*` and `next/root-params`. The bridge
keeps its request store on a global Symbol so every bundled environment
observes the same request.

The RSC `next-intl` hooks call `use()` on the request's single cached config
promise. That promise carries React's `status`/`value`, and
`NextIntlClientProvider` settles it before rendering children, so translated
server components render inline. A hook that suspends makes Flight outline the
component as a lazy row. React's streaming renderer (19.2.8, and still 19.3.1)
can leave a Suspense boundary unresolved when a boundary rendered after the
shell has a fallback that suspends. The browser then reports React error #419.
Keep Suspense fallbacks synchronous. A translated server component rendered
above or beside the provider still suspends once; in development the bridge
logs a one-time `console.warn` for it.

Assert emitted HTML with `findUnresolvedSuspenseBoundaries` from
`@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/suspense-boundaries`; it must return `[]`. It
reports:
- pending boundaries, under any `identifierPrefix`;
- completions whose segment container (`div`, `svg`, `math` or table) is missing;
- unfilled `P:` segments;
- boundaries switched to client rendering (`$RX`, or `<!--$!-->` from the shell).

It reads the inline instruction scripts of stable React and the `data-r*i`
templates of the external runtime.

## Runtime tag

Cutovers are direct, with an instant one-step rollback prepared before the
flip and a post-deploy watch (see the native Start migration runbook); there
are no staged canaries. Tag every native response with `x-tuturuuu-runtime:
native` (`RUNTIME_HEADER`; `tagResponse` with a `native` decision) so the
watch can tell native traffic from the prior deployment. The cohort helpers
in `canary` (`decideCohort`, `TUTURUUU_NATIVE_CANARY_PERCENT`) are retained
but unused.

## Vite preset

```ts
const bridge = startBridgePreset({
  appRoot: import.meta.url,
  app: 'apps',
  navigation: 'document',
  shims: ['next/headers', 'next/server', 'next/navigation', 'next/link', 'next-intl'],
  serverOnlySpecifiers: ['@tuturuuu/satellite/auth'],
});
export default defineConfig(({ command }) => ({
  base: bridge.base,
  define: bridge.define,
  experimental: bridge.experimental,
  plugins: [voidPlugin(), tanstackStart(bridge.tanstackStart), react(), tailwindcss()],
  environments: { client: { define: bridge.clientDefine(command) } },
  resolve: { alias: bridge.alias },
}));
```

`basePath` defaults to `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH` at build time. List `shims`
explicitly when converting an app whose current config aliases only some
`next/*` modules, so the bundle does not change.

Worker SSR/RSC environments resolve `workerd`, `worker`, `module` and `browser`
export conditions, matching Cloudflare's runtime. A package whose `browser`
entry needs a DOM therefore fails during server rendering, and its `node` entry
is no substitute when it depends on jsdom. Do not reorder conditions per package;
use a DOM-free implementation for code that renders on the server. For example,
`isomorphic-dompurify` throws at import and `dompurify` has no `sanitize`
without a `window`, so server-rendered rich text uses `sanitize-html` (Forms,
Mail). Cover the swap with a `@vitest-environment node` test that mocks the
DOM-only module to throw.

## CI template

`.github/workflows/native-start-app.yaml` is the reusable validation for a
bridged app. Each app keeps a thin caller (`<app>-cloudflare.yaml`) that owns
the triggers, the **path filters** (the app, every workspace package in its
dependency closure including `packages/start-bridge/**`, its artifact helper,
`bun.lock`, the caller and the template), concurrency and the `ci-check.yml`
gate, then calls the template with:

| Input | Example (Shortener) |
| --- | --- |
| `app`, `package` | `shortener`, `@tuturuuu/shortener` |
| `artifact-script` | `scripts/ci/shortener-native-artifact.py` (config/seal/verify/pack/restore) |
| `env-interface`, `worker-environment-type` | `ShortenerGeneratedEnv`, `ShortenerEnvironment` |
| `public-env` | Newline-separated `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`/`TUTURUUU_NOINDEX` build fixtures; anything else is rejected |
| `format-paths` | Owning paths for Biome |
| `helper-tests`, `unit-command`, `runtime-command` | Optional overrides |
| `runtime-setup-command` | Optional prerequisite install (for example Playwright browsers) run in its own 10-minute step before each runtime step, so slow mirrors cannot consume the tight runtime timeout |

Runtime setup uses `.github/actions/install-native-runtime-prerequisites` in
both validation and restore acceptance. On the disposable Ubuntu runner it
keeps Ubuntu's suites, components and signing key, selects the official HTTPS
archive instead of the Azure mirror, and sets three apt acquisition retries
with 20-second HTTP/HTTPS inactivity timeouts. Index download failures are
fatal. The existing ten-minute setup and four-minute runtime limits remain.
Playwright still owns the complete Chromium/font dependency list and already
uses `--no-install-recommends`; do not trim fonts to hide download failures.
No package cache or whole-command replay is used. For a setup timeout, inspect
the apt download host and timestamps separately from browser installation;
then rerun the failed job after resolving transport failures. Regression coverage:
`node --test scripts/ci/native-runtime-prerequisites.test.js`.

The template validates the inputs and runs, on the exact source SHA: frozen
install, dependency build, build identity, the registry check, unit tests,
Biome, the Void build, route-tree drift, type-check, emitted-config validation,
emitted binding-type compatibility (a scoped harness: the generated bindings
become a module importing only the Workers types they name, checked under the
app's own tsconfig, so global runtime types never retype app code), Wrangler `deploy --dry-run`, then seal →
emitted runtime → verify → pack. A second job restores the archive into clean
output and repeats the dry-run, runtime acceptance and byte verification. It
has no publish job or provider credential; production stays held in
`tuturuuu.ci.ts`. Apps with extra acceptance (Apps' browser anchors, Meet's
realtime Worker) keep those steps in their own workflow until the template
grows an input for them.

## Verification

`packages/start-bridge` unit tests cover each core module and adapter at the
root and under `/meet`, plus the ported Meet proxy-bridge regressions. App
adoption still needs that app's exact-commit CI: unit, type-check, lint,
`vp build`, the sealed artifact and emitted-runtime acceptance where the app
has them.
